3. There is no evidence provided in the queries to suggest that Breitbart News published this specific report. Furthermore, mainstream investigative reports (Q2, A2) state there is no evidence for the broader claim regarding child pornography on the laptop. statements.statement: Breitbart News did not publish a report claiming that Senator Chris Coons' daughter and seven other underage girls were featured on Hunter Biden's laptop, and a representative from Breitbart confirmed that the website had not published the specific allegation, which was made by Lauren Witzke, a Republican nominee challenging Senator Coons, during an interview on a Breitbart radio show, rather than being a report by Breitbart itself.
statements.support_span: The claim cannot be found anywhere on Breitbart.com and a representative of the conservative publisher confirmed to Lead Stories that the website never published such a report. | Next, we emailed Breitbart.com's executive staff and got a quick reply. No, they assured us, Breitbart had not published the claim. | The Republican running against Coons for Delaware's senate seat did make the allegation during an interview on a Breitbart radio show, but the representative said Breitbart was not reporting it and had not confirmed it.

statements.statement: Lauren Witzke made the claim on the 'Breitbart News Saturday' radio show on SiriusXM on October 24, 2020, citing anonymous sources, and a Facebook meme circulated on October 24, 2020, falsely attributing the claim to Breitbart News.
statements.support_span: We did find Lauren Witzke, the Republican nominee challenging Sen. Coons in the November election, made the claim while being interviewed by "Breitbart News Saturday" on SiriusXM radio on Saturday, October 24, 2020. | The claim appeared in a meme in a post... shared on Facebook on October 24 2020. The meme read: The daughter of Sen. Coons (D-DE), along with 7 other underage girls are featured on Hunter's laptop! - Breitbart News

silver.justification: The evidence indicates that Breitbart News did not publish a report containing the allegation regarding Senator Chris Coons' daughter; a Breitbart representative explicitly confirmed that the website never published such a claim. While the allegation was indeed made by Republican nominee Lauren Witzke during an interview on a Breitbart radio show, the evidence clarifies that this was a guest's statement rather than an official report by the news organization. Furthermore, the evidence suggests the false attribution to Breitbart News originated from a Facebook meme that circulated around the same time the interview aired.
